newsitem.title: CANADA: PanCanadian makes Timor Sea oil find.
newsitem.headline: PanCanadian makes Timor Sea oil find.

text.p: PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd said on Tuesday an offshore well it drilled off the western coast of Australia tested light oil at a rate of 7,600 barrels a day.

The well, Tenacious-1 ST1 on exploration permit AC/P17 in the Timor Sea, was its second discovery in the region in two months, said Calgary-based PanCanadian, which has a 25 percent interest in the play.
Other partners include operator Cultus Petroleum NL of Australia, Japan's Cosmo Oil Co Ltd and Gulf Canada Resources Ltd.
PanCanadian said the well encountered an oil column of 39.5 metres in the Upper Jurassic Tithonian Sandstone at a depth of 2,808 metres.
A drillstem test flowed 7,667 barrels a day of 49 degree API gravity oil and 4.02 million cubic feet of natural gas, it said.
The company also said the maximum flow rate was limited by the 3-1/2 inch tubing used for the test.
The discovery followed another well, Woolybutt-1, located 44 km west of Barrow Island, which in May flowed at 7,600 barrels a day.

"This second discovery, so close on the heels of our Woolybutt discovery, demonstrates further success in PanCanadian's international exploration program, as well as the quality of our Australian portfolio," PanCanadian vice-president Paul Ellis said in a statment.
